newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa to probe Palme murder allegation.
newsitem.headline: South Africa to probe Palme murder allegation.

text.p: South Africa will conduct a full investigation of charges that an apartheid police spy was behind the assassination 10 years ago of Swedish Prime Minister Olof Palme, a state lawyer said on Friday.
Antoinette de Jager, a member of the attorney-general's staff, was responding to court testimony on Thursday by Eugene de Kock, former head of a now disbanded police hit squad.
"All claims made by Mr de Kock will thoroughly investigated, but I do not want to discuss the details of his allegations," de Jager said in a telephone interview.
De Kock said in court he had volunteered information on various apartheid-era crimes to de Jager, including the involvement of former spy Craig Williamson in Palme's 1986 murder.
Williamson, one of the white minority government's most effective agents during the 1970s and 1980s, has admitted to carrying out bombings and other actions against anti-apartheid activists.

He is reported to be in Angola and has made no comment on the statements by de Kock, who made the remarks in court in a plea for a lenient sentence after being convicted of six murders and a series of other crimes.
Prosecutor Anton Ackermann quizzed de Kock about the Palme murder on Friday, asking him if he was repeating hearsay reports.
"I have first-hand information," de Kock replied. He said he had first learned of Williamson's role in the killing in 1992 or 1993.
De Kock denied making the revelation in an attempt to manipulate the press or divert attention from his own criminal activities.
Ackermann asked him if he had any information about the assassination of U.S. President John F. Kennedy. "No, I was too young at the time," de Kock replied.
A spokesman for the Swedish embassy in South Africa said de Kock's testimony had been passed on to Stockholm.
Detectives there said on Thursday the testimony could provide a fresh lead in the still unsolved murder.
"A part of the de Kock information is new. I do not want to say what is new to us and what is not," Lars Jonsson, deputy of the police investigation, told the national news agency TT.
Palme was an enthusiastic supporter of the African National Congress (ANC), a banned liberation movement until 1990, and a staunch opponent of apartheid.

The ANC under Nelson Mandela won South Africa's first all-race election in 1994. Since then members of the former secret police have testified in various court cases of apartheid-era dirty tricks against opponents or critics of the white minority government.
